annotations.title: Daily guides for an app's website

description: Use this when the user asks about the guides Apptiller writes for their app's website. Daily guides for one app's website: whether they're on and what's missing to turn them on (a verified website in a connected Search Console, and a plan that includes them), and its guides, newest first. Each guide answers one need no page on the site answers: Google searches that show the site but are rarely clicked (the search and its numbers), a question Google's AI answers leave the app out of (its answers), or both. finding_id is the To do item's finding it was written for and finding_ids all of that item's findings (empty for guides written before items had findings): the need behind it, the title, address slug, meta description, the guide in Markdown with its two calls to action, the sentences to add on the site's own pages to link to it, and every claim the check read with what backs it (status held: something couldn't be backed; fix it before publishing). agent_spec is the whole job for a coding agent: where the page goes, its head tags and structured data, the links to add, the checks. Published guides carry their Google clicks and impressions since. Guides written from research also carry research (what they were written from, each part with its source and date or why it is missing: the site's Search Console searches on the topic, its App Store search terms, labelled as App Store demand and not Google volume, the tracked AI questions, the product's facts, the site's pages, Google's results and the top pages read, and Google search volume and difficulty), plan (the target searches by research id, the sections and the searches each serves, internal links from the site's pages, the FAQ), watch (the Google searches it targets) and, once published, watched (each of those searches' clicks, impressions and position on its address since). readiness.last_run says how the last morning run ended: a guide, the fix for a page's search finding drafted instead (its finding id), nothing and why, or an error. Apptiller never publishes them.
